classes.found: acip: ,AI Dm GU RU RA{tn} MAnd LA Km NI{ry}'A TA YA MI, ,   |   wylie: ai dM gu ru ra maND la kM ni'a ta ya mi,
classes.expected: The Wylie should carry the braced Sanskrit stacks the ACIP encodes: "ratna" (from RA{tn}) and "nirya" (from NI{ry}). Cf. the same mantra at TCS07:82, which is intact: "ai daM gu ru ratna maNDa la kaM niryA ta yA mi".
classes.evidence: The seg_hint of 40 is WRONG: C01:40 is the Pabongka title colophon ("rdo rje 'chang pha bong kha pa..."). The described strings (dM/kM/ND capitals, ni'a ta ya mi, ra maND la kM) occur at C01:6, verified verbatim. The ACIP source is CORRECT — {tn} and {ry} are the ACIP escapes for Sanskrit stacks, as at C01:344 (BU{ddh} P'A LI TA = Buddhapalita). The derived Wylie column silently drops the braced content: C01:6 "ra maND la" loses tn, "ni'a" loses ry. The parallel English in the same segment prints the correct "Idam guru ratna mandalakam niryatayami" twice, and TCS07:82 carries the undamaged Wylie.
classes.note: Systematic, not local: the same converter loss produces "bu pA li ta" for Buddhapalita at C01:344 (HIGH severity there — a reader is taught a wrong author name with no adjacent correction), and leaks raw braces at C03:351 ("a{u2} Ta'i" from Sm {bh}A{u2} tA'I). Scored MEDIUM here only because C01:6's own English line supplies the correct reading inches away. The fix belongs in the ACIP-to-Wylie conversion, not in the source text. The trailing "COVERAGE GATE: C01 474->477; 19 open" in the note is campaign bookkeeping and carries no erratum.

classes.evidence: Verified in build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db, row id=867. C03:303 stores wylie='the preliminaries' (17 chars, confirmed with length(wylie)) and english='I. Why the Steps?' (17 chars); the acip column holds 'THE PRELIMINARIES' — English sitting in the transliteration column — and raw carries the same. The wylie is not Wylie: 'preliminaries' has no legal syllable analysis ('prel' is not a possible stack, 'aries' has no root-letter reading). Three courses carry the IDENTICAL wylie against unrelated English, which proves the string is a repeated editorial running head rather than any segment's text: C01:43 'the preliminaries' / 'I. The Lama and the Word'; C09:171 'the preliminaries' / 'The preliminary division of my text has two parts of its own: the offering of praise, and an identification of that which is to be to be explained.'; C03:303 / 'I. Why the Steps?'. The mechanism is visible where the same header stream was concatenated in front of real Tibetan instead of being stranded alone: C03:298 wylie = "how the teaching was given ,de la 'dir khyab bdag 'khor lo'i mgon po rdo rje 'chang..." and C09:54 wylie = "i. the preliminaries de la 'dir rje btsun chos kyi rgyal po shar tsong kha pa chen po blo...". Sibling header rows of the same class in this course: C03:22 'the asian classics institute'; C03:294 'foreword'; C03:295 'about the authors'; C03:401 'steps shared with those of lesser capacity'; C03:430 'steps shared with those of medium capacity'; C03:476 'open steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:513 'secret steps for those of greater capacity'; C03:558 'the conclusion'. Class boundary, to prevent over-broad remediation: C03:263 wylie='the tshom' / english='Destructive Doubts vi.' IS genuine Wylie (the tshom = doubt) and is NOT part of this class. Effect: the segment carries no Tibetan, so it cannot be aligned, and wylie-side FTS or concordance queries return English strings as though they were Tibetan. No textual correction is possible — the remedy is reclassification as an editorial section header rather than a Tibetan-English parallel segment.

classes.evidence: CLASS ENTRY, not a single instance. Printed footnote reference numbers have been flattened into the running English at ingest, fused to the sentence-final period with no separator. Measured across the whole spine: 307 occurrences in 281 segments across 5 courses - C01 161, C03 95, C16 38, TCS13 7, TCS15 6. Counted on the signature 'sentence-final punctuation + 1-3 digits + space + capital', which excludes thousands separators ('25,000'), section labels ('(S1)') and verse citations ('[I.1b]'); two looser patterns were tried first and gave 1,054 and 867 before those contaminants were excluded. Every instance breaks exact-match search on the final word of its sentence.

classes.expected: the whole English of the segment; a segment whose translation runs past 1,500 characters loses its tail with no marker, no count and no log line
classes.evidence: Found by the skeptic pass on C03:429 (E-106), which asked why that field ends mid-sentence at 'there are five ' and measured length(english) = 1500 exactly. Census 2026-09-01 on build/hgm_spine_v27_2.db: 186 segments have length(english) = 1500 (DDA 28, C18 15, C12 14, C13 12, C11 11, Sunlight 11, C17 10, C03 9 - including C03:376, 429, 620, the Reading Eight/Nine/Ten note blocks - MB2 8, C16 7, and 25 further courses); 34 segments EXCEED 1,500, so at least one ingest path does not apply the cap and its reach is not uniform. What is lost is not always apparatus: wherever the cap falls inside a translation, the corpus has no English for the rest of the Tibetan and nothing can align it. The 186 are a floor for the affected rows (a row cut at exactly the cap is certain; a row that happened to be shorter is unaffected).
classes.note: OURS, NOT FIXED. The cap lives in the canonical ingest (engines/hgm_tools.py), so removing it changes the spine itself and must be re-proved against the full batteries (inviolable rule 2) before any layer is rebuilt on it; the C03:376/429/620 note blocks and any truncated translation would need re-scanning afterwards. Opened in TODO.md 2026-09-01 for Adam's ruling and the data project. No document edit is asked of ALL for this entry - it is a pipeline defect on our side.
